mission.summary: Turn the ThinkPad L540 into a portable command station for a scout (e-bike, drone, radio, Android with ATAK) that can listen to the radio world (aircraft, ships, weather, mesh), know exactly where it is on offline Puerto Rico maps, coordinate a small team over off-grid LoRa mesh, and control what it transmits so it stays as quiet as possible on networks and airwaves.
mission.scenario_framing: Grid-down / emergency preparedness role-play the owner finds motivating ('special recon in a SHTF scenario'). Treat it as a learning and preparedness project: receive-only sensing, the owner's own equipment, legal transmitting only.
principles: Offline first: everything works with zero internet; updates only in LINK mode
Silent by default: nothing transmits unless the operator chooses a mode that allows it
Receive is legal and invisible; transmit is a decision (EMCON modes)
Encrypted at rest; the owner's data never leaves the deck except by choice
Beginner-operable: one command per box, every screen explains itself in Spanish and English
Legal only (see legal_lines) - the project must never become a problem for the owner

owner_profile_and_working_style.skill: Beginner learning Linux; investor/business owner, not a programmer. Visual learner. Wants independence from AI over time.
owner_profile_and_working_style.commands: He TYPES every terminal command by hand. Always give commands as single lines, ONE per code box, numbered in order, and for each say what to look for, what he should see and what to expect.
owner_profile_and_working_style.build_model: 80/20: the AI builds and pushes to GitHub; he runs `git pull` and the setup on the ThinkPad and reports back with photos.
owner_profile_and_working_style.language: Bilingual UI and docs: Spanish primary, English secondary (same as El Cacique).
owner_profile_and_working_style.budget: Limited. Work from what he owns first; add only what's needed for a base he can expand. Prefer TP-Link for network gear. The Deeper (Connect Mini at home, Connect Pico in the field) is non-negotiable in his setups.
owner_profile_and_working_style.autostart: Nothing starts by itself at boot unless he chooses it (installer checkbox, off by default). Exception pattern exists in El Cacique: an always-on health page he explicitly chose.
owner_profile_and_working_style.values: No surveillance, data ownership, open source, no accounts with third parties, legal content only.

the_base.os: Ubuntu (LTS) on the internal drive - the friendly command station. Same family as El Cacique.
the_base.role: Maps, GPS, Meshtastic, SDR sensing, ATAK link + OpenTAKServer, drone ground station, logbook, field library, the VU HUD.
the_base.encryption: Ubuntu was installed unencrypted. Plan: (a) when the SSD arrives, reinstall with full-disk LUKS encryption (preferred), or (b) until then, encrypt the user data with an encrypted home/data volume. Ask the owner which and when.
hardening: ufw default deny incoming; allow nothing inbound except the USB-tethered phone subnet and localhost services
NetworkManager: MAC address randomization for Wi-Fi scans and connections; generic hostname; no auto-join of networks
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi hardware-off with rfkill in SILENT mode
USBGuard (allow-list of the owner's devices; new USB devices blocked until approved)
AppArmor on (Ubuntu default); unattended upgrades only in LINK mode
Tor Browser for any online lookups; no cloud accounts or telemetry on the deck
Ledger FIDO2/U2F for any logins that support it; OpenPGP for signing/encrypting field notes
Encrypted 'drop' partition (on the Overkill stick) is the only data bridge between Base and Overkill

the_overkill.os: Kali Linux Live + LUKS-encrypted persistence on the 256 GB stick (boot option 'Live USB Encrypted Persistence'); Kali nuke passphrase tested on a copy first; LUKS header backup kept at home.
partitions: encrypted 'drop' (~40 GB, LUKS, opened by both Base and Overkill)
the_overkill.role: Ethical-hacking / network-defense LEARNING lab on the owner's own equipment: Nmap, Wireshark, Kismet, Bettercap, aircrack-ng suite, Metasploit, Burp, Hashcat, etc. Practice targets: his own home lab, his own test router, intentionally vulnerable practice VMs.
the_overkill.internal_drive: Not mounted when the Overkill is booted (Base untouched).

system_architecture.optional_ghost_stick: Separate small Tails USB for anonymous browsing via Tor. Not part of the build unless the owner asks.

emcon_modes.description: One command `vu mode silent|mesh|link` + a HUD indicator. Same on Base and Overkill.
emcon_modes.SILENT: Nothing transmits: Wi-Fi + Bluetooth hardware-off (rfkill), Meshtastic node set receive-only (lora.tx_enabled=false), SiK/drone uplink off, phone tethered by cable only. Allowed: GPS, SDR receive, maps, logbook, listening to the mesh.
emcon_modes.MESH: Only short encrypted LoRa bursts when the operator sends; no automatic position beacons (Meshtastic position broadcast off or manual).
emcon_modes.LINK: Wi-Fi allowed (known networks only, e.g. home); updates, sync to El Cacique; Deeper Pico by cable as firewall/VPN.
emcon_modes.always: Random MACs, generic hostname, no network auto-join, phone in airplane mode + Faraday pouch when unused.

modules.what: The main local web app (served on localhost only, stdlib Python like caciquedash.py or a small FastAPI if justified) opened full-screen in Firefox kiosk mode. Tabs/screens below. Works offline.
screens: MAPA/MAP (center: offline PR map with own GPS, mesh nodes, aircraft, ships, drone, waypoints)
SEÑALES/SIGINT (spectrum waterfall link to SDR++, ADS-B list, AIS list, weather)
COMMS (Meshtastic channels, messages, node list, radio state)
NAV (GPS fix, coordinates in MGRS + lat/long, heading, speed, satellites, offline routing)
ESTADO/STATUS (EMCON mode, battery, power source, temps, CPU/RAM, drives, connected gear)
BITÁCORA/LOG (time-stamped field log; export to the encrypted drop)

modules.what: Offline vector + raster maps of Puerto Rico (incl. Vieques and Culebra): OpenStreetMap data (Geofabrik puerto-rico extract) served locally (e.g. tileserver-gl or PMTiles with a local MapLibre front end); terrain/elevation hillshade; optional USGS topo; satellite imagery only where license allows. Same tiles exported for ATAK (MBTiles) so the phone works offline. Organic Maps already tested by the owner as a fallback.
gpsd + u-blox puck; time sync from GPS (chrony) when offline; position feeds the HUD, ATAK (via OpenTAKServer) and optionally Meshtastic (only in MESH/LINK, manual).

Meshtastic Python API/CLI over USB serial; US 915 MHz region; private encrypted channel(s) with owner-chosen PSK (never committed); receive-only toggle for SILENT; message/node view in the HUD; TAK<->Meshtastic gateway so ATAK sees mesh positions/messages.

RTL-SDR stack: SDR++ (spectrum), readsb + tar1090 (ADS-B aircraft, offline map), AIS-catcher (ships; VHF 161.975/162.025 MHz), rtl_433 (weather stations/sensors), NOAA Weather Radio (162.4-162.55 MHz) audio, SatDump (NOAA/Meteor weather satellites), public FRS/GMRS/marine listening in the clear. Feeds aircraft/ships into the HUD map and into TAK as CoT.

OpenTAKServer on the Base (localhost/tether only) or FreeTAKServer if lighter; ATAK-CIV on the Pixel/GrapheneOS connected by USB cable (USB tethering or reverse tethering), Wi-Fi/Bluetooth off on the phone; PyTAK bridges: ADS-B/AIS/drone/mesh -> CoT. Data packages for map sources and the team channel.

QGroundControl (missions, geofence, RTH, telemetry, offline maps); SiK 915 MHz link (MESH/LINK modes only; pre-planned missions can fly with uplink off); MAVLink -> TAK bridge (PyTAK) puts the drone on everyone's map; photo geotag import into the log.
Kismet in PASSIVE mode only: how many devices/networks are around (awareness), nothing joined or attacked. On the Overkill stick for the learning lab; optional on Base.
Kiwix with medical, survival, repair (iFixit), Wikipedia ES/EN subsets that fit the drive; the VU field manual as a ZIM like El Cacique's manual.

JSONL time-stamped log (pattern from El Cacique tools/logbook.py): mode changes, GPS fixes, mesh messages, contacts seen (aircraft/ships), notes; secrets masked; exportable to the encrypted drop; never uploaded.

One-line bootstrap from GitHub + a Tkinter wizard reusing El Cacique's engine pattern (scan -> choose modules -> summary -> install with live log -> finish), restyled in the tactical HUD look. Hardware scan detects gear by USB ID and marks modules ready/missing. Dry-run mode. Every step safe to re-run. Separate script set to prepare the Overkill stick (with explicit 'type yes' confirmations before touching any drive, showing size/model).

security_and_privacy.goal: Protect the deck and its operator: encrypted storage, minimal emissions, no telemetry, controlled USB, and a hands-on LEARNING lab for network defense on the owner's own gear.
must: Full-disk or data encryption (LUKS) on Base; encrypted persistence + drop on Overkill
No secrets in the repo: PSKs, passwords, Ledger data, home coordinates, IPs stay in local .env/keyrings
Firewall default-deny; local services bind to 127.0.0.1 or the USB tether interface only
EMCON modes actually enforce radio state (verify with rfkill list, nmcli, meshtastic --info)
Updates only in LINK mode; verify package signatures (apt/Kali repos)
Teach as you build: each hardening step explained in the field manual
security_and_privacy.learning_lab_rules: Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/network testing ONLY on equipment the owner owns or has written permission to test; a 'lab notebook' template records scope and permission.

legal_lines: Listening to clear (unencrypted) public radio: OK (ADS-B, AIS, NOAA, FRS/GMRS/marine in the clear).
Do NOT intercept cellular calls, decode private encrypted communications, or break into networks - the deck does not do it and the build must not add tools aimed at that.
Transmitting: Meshtastic (915 MHz ISM) and SiK radios are license-free within FCC Part 15 limits; GMRS needs a license (no exam, covers family); amateur bands need an exam.
Jamming or spoofing (RF, GPS, Wi-Fi deauth against others) is illegal - never build it.
Drones: FAA rules - registration, Remote ID on, below 400 ft, out of restricted airspace (B4UFLY); non-recreational use needs Part 107.
Recording people: follow Puerto Rico privacy law; never publish others' data.
The owner stated: not asking to find, hack, crack, download or make anything illegal.

conventions.commit_trailer: End commit messages with the attribution lines the session provides.
conventions.secrets: Never commit .env, PSKs, passwords, IPs, family names, coordinates. Use .gitignore + local files with chmod 600.
conventions.style: Plain words in docs; ES first, EN second; no jargon without a one-line explanation.
conventions.testing: Simulate hardware with mocks (fake serial, recorded ADS-B/AIS samples, fake gpsd) and say plainly what still needs the real device.

naming_research_note: Owner first asked for a Taíno name meaning 'Shadow Warrior/Hunter'. Taíno survives only in colonial records: no attested words for 'hunter' or 'shadow'; closest were hupia (night spirit of the dead, hides by day, linked to bats) and nitaíno (noble class that led in war). Owner chose Latin instead: Venator Umbrae. Taíno words may still appear as module nicknames if he wants (e.g. Hupia for SILENT mode).
